title: A Crown of Thorns
lines: In the thirty-second year of her marriage, Empress Navier discovered that her husband, Emperor Sovieshu, intended to divorce her. Not for politics, not for statecraft, but for a woman he had met at a hunting lodge three months prior. A commoner.

Navier did not weep. She did not scream. She called her lady-in-waiting and ordered tea service for the afternoon sessions of the Grand Council, as she had done every day for thirty-two years. The empire would not see its empress falter.

But in her private chambers, with the door bolted and the curtains drawn, Navier removed her crown — the heavy golden headpiece she had worn since her coronation at sixteen — and held it in her lap like a dead child.
'I accept,' she told the emperor the next morning, her voice steady as marble. 'I accept the divorce on one condition: I will choose the man I remarry.'

Sovieshu agreed, certain no man of rank would accept a divorced empress. He was wrong. On the day the divorce was finalized, seven letters of proposal arrived at Navier's palace — including one sealed with the griffin crest of the neighboring kingdom, sent by a king whose name Navier had never heard.
